concepts.name: Amazon MSK
concepts.text: Managed Apache Kafka in your VPC; Provisioned for full config control (with tiered storage & Express brokers) or Serverless for automatic scaling.

concepts.name: MSK Connect
concepts.text: Runs managed Kafka Connect source and sink connectors (e.g., Debezium CDC from databases or S3 sinks) with no Connect cluster to manage.

concepts.name: Managed Flink
concepts.tag: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
concepts.text: Managed Apache Flink (Java, Scala, Python, SQL) for keyed state, windows, stream joins, event-time watermarks, and checkpointed fault tolerance.

concepts.name: Kafka Core Model
concepts.text: Topics split into ordered partitions (parallelism unit); record keys enforce per-partition ordering, and consumer groups track offsets.

rows: existing Kafka producers/consumers, minimal code changes
Kafka APIs with no cluster sizing or broker management
windowed aggregation, stream joins, exactly-once, event time
deliver MSK topic data to S3 with no code
very long retention of stream data cheaply
MSK tiered storage (or archive to S3)

diagram.heading: MSK ingestion, Flink analytics & S3 landing

items.label: Ingest to MSK
items.text: Producers or MSK Connect (Debezium CDC) write keyed records into Kafka topic partitions.

items.label: Stateful Process
items.text: Managed Service for Apache Flink computes windows, dedup, or joins using checkpoints and watermarks.

items.label: Deliver & Serve
items.text: Write results to OpenSearch dashboards, or land MSK topics to S3 (Firehose / sink) and Redshift MVs.

table.heading: Kafka vs. Kinesis Mapping
rows: Consumer's read position in a partition
Time/size-based; very long with tiered storage

tips: Choose MSK only when Kafka compatibility is required; otherwise Kinesis Data Streams has less operational overhead.
Flink is not a delivery service and Firehose is not a stateful processor; watch for distractors that swap them.
"Kinesis Data Analytics" is the former name for Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink.
MSK runs inside your VPC: consumers (Lambda, Glue, EMR) need VPC network access and proper security group rules.
